FINDING_ID: F001  
SEVERITY: 0.98  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer._solve_greedy()` can deliberately return allocations that violate HARD feasibility constraint F1 by force-assigning a task even when every admissible model would exceed token limits. The code comment acknowledges this: “F1 violation is reported but coverage is maintained.” That contradicts the stated model, where F1 is a HARD constraint, and also contradicts the load-balancing description that feasibility constraints are enforced. This is not just heuristic degradation; it is implementation of an infeasible allocation as if it were a valid solution.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Do not force-assign when no feasible assignee exists. Return an explicit infeasible result/state, or raise a structured exception / status object indicating coverage target could not be met under HARD constraints. If soft degradation is desired, reclassify F1 in the model/docs as soft under a documented fallback mode.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002  
SEVERITY: 0.95  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` calls `health_monitor.record_model_round(mid, fc, failed)` with `failed = mid not in responses or not responses[mid].parseable`. This misclassifies TIMEOUT, EMPTY, and FORMAT failures as non-failures whenever `parseable=True` or a response object exists. The immune layer’s consecutive failure detection for `model_failure` therefore undercounts real failures and can miss escalation/remediation entirely. This breaks the intended immune integration between failure handling and detector health monitoring.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Derive `failed` from the actual detected `failure_type is not None`, or at minimum from failure types in `{EMPTY, TIMEOUT, MALFORMED, FORMAT}`. Pass response time/char count too so the immune monitor evaluates the real response.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003  
SEVERITY: 0.93  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` emits `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED` for FORMAT violations instead of `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION`. This breaks the documented event-type interface and makes downstream monitoring unable to distinguish malformed responses from parseable-but-format-noncompliant ones. Since the event stream is part of the public monitoring interface, this is an observable correctness bug.  
PROPOSED_FIX: In the FORMAT branch, emit `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION`. Add a regression test asserting distinct event types for MALFORMED vs FORMAT.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004  
SEVERITY: 0.92  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.86  
DESCRIPTION: The code does not implement several mathematical model factors that the appendix claims are part of the effective detection process: `f_del`, `η_dec`, and `φ_i`. The appendix explicitly states combined effective detection probability `q_ik = f_del(i) · φ_i · d_ik · p_ik`, and decomposition-adjusted `q_ik^dec = η_dec(i) · d_ik · p_ik`. In the code, none of these quantities are represented in the mathematical layer or fed into coverage/risk computations. The immune layer contains heuristic detectors loosely related to delivery failure and parser yield, but those are not implementation of the appendix formulas. This is a traceability/model-implementation mismatch.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either (a) update `MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md`/traceability to mark these formulas as not yet implemented, or (b) add explicit state/estimation for `f_del`, `η_dec`, `φ_i` and incorporate them into the relevant detection/coverage calculations rather than only into heuristic diagnosis.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005  
SEVERITY: 0.91  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor.false_positive_rate` claims “last 10 rounds” behavior but divides recent natural resolutions by essentially all historical detections. `total_detections` is not filtered by round window, while `natural_resolutions` is. This biases the rate downward over time and defeats the self-diagnosis trigger for high false-positive rate.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Store diagnosis round explicitly and compute both numerator and denominator over the same rolling window.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: `VerificationChain.verify_inclusion_proof()` ignores the `merkle_root` embedded in the proof object and instead verifies against the caller-supplied root string. That is acceptable only if the caller already authenticates the external root, but the method name and docstring imply proof verification against “a given Merkle root” without checking consistency with proof contents. This enables silent acceptance of a proof object whose internal `merkle_root` disagrees with the supplied root, weakening integrity expectations and making malformed proofs harder to detect.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate that `proof["merkle_root"]` exists and equals the supplied `merkle_root` when present, or remove `merkle_root` from the proof structure entirely to avoid ambiguity.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F007  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_model_round()` supports `response_time` and `response_chars`, but `DynamicManager.process_round()` never passes them. As a result, parser-yield anomaly detection (`response_chars > tau_chars and finding_count == 0`) and cost-per-finding spike detection are effectively disabled or severely degraded. The interface exists, but the integration is incomplete.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass `responses[mid].response_time` and `len(responses[mid].content)` when available; pass zero only when the response is absent.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F008  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: `VerificationChain._verify_single()` only recomputes `payload_hash` when `storage_mode == "full_payload"`. In `hash_only` mode, the stored `payload_hash` is never structurally validated beyond inclusion in the entry hash. An invalid digest format like `"not-a-digest"` would still pass chain verification if consistently sealed. That weakens the stated contract that `payload_hash` is a cryptographic payload digest.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Always validate `sealed_body["payload_hash"]` with `_digest_bytes()` or equivalent format checking, even in `hash_only` mode.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F009  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector._compute_equivalence_classes()` uses single-linkage clustering over pairwise similarity threshold. The appendix/model language treats equivalence classes as if they are genuine equivalence classes under `≈`, but thresholded similarity is generally not transitive. Single-linkage can therefore merge findings A~B and B~C even when A and C are dissimilar, inflating class aggregation, suppressing novelty, and overstating convergence.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either document that this is a heuristic connected-components approximation rather than an equivalence relation, or replace it with a clustering rule consistent with the mathematical assumption needed by downstream formulas.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F010  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.81  
DESCRIPTION: The mathematical appendix states in §6 that `C_M(k) = 1 − Π(1 − d_M,i · p_M,i,k) — machine cumulative detection (= F_n)`. That equality is only true if `F_n` is interpreted per class or without the outer `Σ_k w_k`. The appendix mixes per-class and aggregated quantities. The code does not implement `G_n`, but the documentation itself is internally inconsistent and therefore not traceable to code.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rewrite the definition as `C_M(k)` is the per-class term inside `F_n`, not `F_n` itself. Update any traceability table accordingly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F011  
SEVERITY: 0.85  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` updates `self.capability_scores[mid][Role.COL.value]` with failure-penalized adjusted scores, but PM and PAR scores remain stale initial values. This means `capability_scores` becomes a mixed structure: some entries are live/penalized, others are static/baseline. Any consumer treating it as a coherent current score table gets inconsistent semantics.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either maintain a separate `live_capability_scores` structure for round-specific penalized scores, or recompute/update all role scores consistently under the same live fingerprint/failure-history basis.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F012  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer._redundancy_target()` uses total `K = len(self.models)`, not the number of admissible or active models for a task. When PM is excluded from standard tasks for `K > 1`, a critical task gets target `K` even though only `K-1` models may be admissible. This guarantees unattainable redundancy targets and repeated degraded allocation warnings by construction.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Base redundancy target on admissible capacity for the task, e.g. `min(desired_target, number_of_admissible_models)` or define the formula in terms of eligible workers rather than total models.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F013  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.7  
DESCRIPTION: `apply_diagnosis()` treats `diagnosis.detector == "verification"` by only adding a per-model directive if that model has no existing directive. If a model already has a directive, the verification remediation is silently skipped rather than merged/appended, even though the diagnosis is active. This can block adaptive correction for exactly the models most likely to already have custom directives.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Merge directives with bounded concatenation/truncation, or maintain structured directive slots per concern instead of single-string overwrite semantics.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F014  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.84  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix defines substantial quantities not implemented anywhere in code within the reviewed areas: `R_n`, `L_n`, `G_n`, `H(x)`, `Y(t)` as defined in §7.3, `V̂(t,T)`, `O_A`, `Δ_adopt/Δ_drop`, `S_v`, and `selected(f)`. Some nearby heuristics exist (`kappa`, `mu`, live fingerprint fields), but they are not faithful implementations of the stated formulas. Without an explicit traceability table marking these as future work, the mathematical model overstates implementation coverage.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an implementation-status / traceability matrix mapping each formula to concrete code symbols, with “not implemented” where applicable.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F015  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68  
DESCRIPTION: `check_dispatch_feasibility()` records dispatch blocks, but successful later decomposed runs are only tracked if some external caller manually invokes `record_dispatch_success_after_block()`. There is no integration in `process_round()` or elsewhere to infer this from actual successful responses. The Phase E false-positive dispatch diagnosis is therefore incomplete and likely underfires.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Integrate success-after-block recording into the normal dispatch/result pipeline, using model_id plus prior block history and successful response presence.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F016  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: `VerificationChain.load_json()` does not validate `schema_version` at all. Chains with incompatible schema versions are loaded silently, and verification then proceeds under current assumptions. For a tamper-evident persistence layer, schema compatibility is part of correctness.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate top-level `schema_version` on load and fail or warn on mismatch. Ideally version-gate deserialization rules.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F017  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.7  
DESCRIPTION: `canonical_json()` warns in the docstring that floats in sealed bodies can break determinism, but the code does not enforce this invariant. Records may therefore be sealed with floats despite the stated prohibition, creating cross-platform reproducibility risk for signatures and hashes.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add recursive validation rejecting floats in sealed bodies/payloads or canonicalize numerics via fixed-precision decimal strings before sealing.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F018  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.75  
DESCRIPTION: `CorrelatedFailureModel` docstring states correlated joint failure as `P(i fails) * P(j fails) + v_ij * min(P(i), P(j))`, but the actual implementation uses `p_i * p_j + v_ij * min(p_i, p_j) * (1 - max(p_i, p_j))`. The implementation is more defensible, but the documentation is wrong. Since the analytical boundary includes math-model verification, this is a formula/code mismatch in a mathematically significant area of the same file.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Update the docstring and any appendix/traceability references to match the implemented bounded formula.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F019  
SEVERITY: 0.77  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` classifies underperformance using `actual = finding_count * mean_abstraction` divided by a baseline computed from raw fingerprint values. This can exceed 1 arbitrarily and is not normalized to a comparable scale with the configured threshold `theta_under = 0.3`. The result is a threshold whose semantics depend strongly on the magnitude conventions of fingerprint fields and finding counts rather than a stable fraction-of-expected-performance interpretation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Normalize actual and expected onto the same bounded scale, or rename/document the metric as an unbounded productivity ratio and recalibrate `theta_under` accordingly.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F020  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: `VerificationChain.seal_epoch()` seals all current records every time, producing cumulative epochs rather than disjoint epoch segments. That is valid if intended, but the docs say “Merkle trees over sealed epochs allow compact inclusion proofs for any individual record” without clarifying whether epochs are incremental snapshots or partitioned batches. This ambiguity matters for operational interpretation and proof size expectations.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Document epoch semantics explicitly. If disjoint epochs are intended, track last sealed index and seal only new records.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F021  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 7  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector._compute_equivalence_classes()` is O(n²) pairwise similarity with potentially expensive tokenization per comparison and no caching. For large finding sets this will scale poorly and can become a practical bottleneck in multi-round operation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Pre-tokenize findings once, cache token/bigram sets, and consider blocking by flaw class plus candidate term overlap before full similarity computation.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F022  
SEVERITY: 0.73  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix §7.7 defines `Sev(f)` in terms of HARD/SOFT class, confidence, and verification value, but the code’s `Finding.severity` is a free numeric field with no implemented derivation from those variables. The same symbol is therefore used for different semantics in docs vs code.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rename code field to `severity_score` with explicit provenance, or implement the appendix severity function and map inputs accordingly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F023  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: `VerificationChain._normalize_timestamp()` accepts naive timestamps and silently interprets them as UTC. That may be operationally convenient, but it weakens the stated meaning of claimed timestamps and can hide timezone mistakes. In a persistence/audit layer, silent timezone coercion is risky.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either reject naive timestamps or require explicit opt-in for assuming UTC.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F024  
SEVERITY: 0.70  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.6  
DESCRIPTION: `apply_diagnosis()` accesses `self.health_monitor._remediation_state` directly. That bypasses the health monitor’s public interface and couples manager logic to internal mutable state. This is an interface integrity problem inside the immune subsystem boundary.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a public accessor/mutator for remediation chain state, e.g. `get_remediation_state()` / `advance_remediation_chain()`, and stop reaching into underscore-prefixed fields.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F025  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: `VerificationChain.verify_chain()` returns success for an empty chain with message “nothing to verify.” That may be acceptable, but for some audit uses an empty chain should be distinguished from a verified non-empty chain. The current API conflates “valid structure” with “evidence exists.”  
PROPOSED_FIX: Keep boolean validity if desired, but expose an explicit status enum or record count so callers cannot mistake emptiness for substantive verification.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

Definitive stance: the highest-confidence defects are the HARD-constraint violation in load balancing, the immune-layer miswiring of failure signals, the malformed event typing, and the substantial appendix↔code traceability gaps. The persistence layer is structurally solid but has several correctness/assurance weaknesses around proof/root consistency, schema validation, and unenforced canonicalization invariants.
